comment: Operator library manifest (#663). Each entry maps a (op_kind, tier, dtype) triple to a compiled SASS blob. The blob path is resolved relative to this manifest's directory. Update this file when adding a new operator/tier/dtype variant; keep in lockstep with enum slm_gpu_op_kind / SLM_GPU_TIER_* / enum slm_gpu_dtype in kernel/include/gpu_handoff.h.

entries.comment: Today's CUDA-core FP32 GEMM. Reads M/K/N from cbuf at dispatch time. Source: scripts/cuda/gemm_fp32.cu.
Direct (no im2col) FP32 conv. Source: scripts/cuda/conv2d_fp32_direct.cu. The HMMA tier-1 sibling for this op landed in #674 (see CONV2D.HMMA.FP16 below).
Add per-channel bias, optional ReLU via launcher cbuf flag. Source: scripts/cuda/add_bias_relu_fp32.cu.
Spatial max pooling. Reads kernel/stride from cbuf. Source: scripts/cuda/maxpool2d_fp32.cu.

FP16/FP16 → FP32 tensor-core GEMM via nvcuda::wmma m16n16k16 (lowers to mma.sync.m16n8k16 on sm_87 GA10B). Reads M/K/N from cbuf at dispatch time, same scalar layout as the SIMT FP32 entry — the launcher just swaps the shader. Source: scripts/cuda/gemm_hmma_fp16.cu (#659/#673).

Implicit-GEMM 2D convolution on tensor cores. Reformulates conv as (K_out, C_in·R·S, N_batch·H_out·W_out) GEMM and computes the im2col B-matrix gather in-shader (no DRAM staging). Source: scripts/cuda/conv2d_hmma_fp16.cu (#662/#674).

Q4_K → FP16 dequantizer. One CUDA block per 144-byte super-block, 256 threads each materializing one FP16 output. Mirrors runtime/src/inference/quant.rs::dequant_q4k_block bit-for-bit (validated against CPU reference on Jetson sm_87 across 1/32/128 super-block harness). First SLM-shaped entry in the operator library; usable as a standalone weight-materialization step and as a stepping-stone before the fused Q4K_DOT / Q4K_GEMM kernels land. Source: scripts/cuda/q4k_dequant_f16.cu (#540).

Per-row root-mean-square layer norm in FP16 with FP32 accumulator. One CUDA block per row, 256 threads per block — strided sum-of-squares + tree reduction → rsqrtf → strided write of x * rms_inv * gamma. Mirrors runtime/src/inference/ops_transformer.rs::rmsnorm; matches the CPU reference within 2 ULPs across Qwen2.5-1.5B (1×1536, 16×1536), Llama-2 (1×4096), and a non-multiple-of-256 tail (1×768). Source: scripts/cuda/rmsnorm_f16.cu (#540).

Element-wise fused SiLU + multiply: out = silu(gate) * up = (gate / (1 + exp(-gate))) * up. The activation step that sits between the gate / up matmuls and the down matmul inside the SwiGLU MLP block. One thread per element, 256-thread blocks; sigmoid in FP32 with __expf (CUDA fast intrinsic). Mirrors runtime/src/inference/ops_transformer.rs::silu_out + the element-wise multiply that follows it inside swiglu_mlp_q. Validated within 2 ULPs across Qwen2.5-1.5B (n=8960), Llama-2 (n=11008), 16-row prefill (n=143360), and a non-multiple-of-256 tail (n=1023). NOTE: this is the element-wise half of SWIGLU (op_kind=6). The full MLP block also needs the gate / up / down matmuls, which will land as future Q4K_DOT entries; the dispatcher composes them. Source: scripts/cuda/swiglu_f16.cu (#540).

Rotary Position Embedding for Q/K vectors. Rotates pairs (vec[2i], vec[2i+1]) by precomputed (cos, sin) factors from a flat FP32 LUT keyed on (token position, pair index). One block per (token, head); one thread per pair; no shared memory, no reductions. GPT-NeoX / Llama / Qwen2 pair-interleave convention. Mirrors runtime/src/inference/ops_transformer.rs::RopeTable::apply. Validated within 2 ULPs across Qwen2.5-1.5B Q (1×12×128), K (1×2×128), prefill (16×12×128), Llama-2 Q (1×32×128), and a 64-dim head (1×8×64); position-0 boundary case is bit-exact. Source: scripts/cuda/rope_f16.cu (#540).

Q4_K-weight × FP16-activation matmul (decode path). Computes out[N] = W[N×K] @ x[K] where W is row-major Q4_K-packed (each row = K/256 super-blocks of 144 B) and out is FP32. One block per output row, 256 threads per block; each thread walks every super-block in its row, dequantizes its element on the fly, multiplies by the matching activation, and accumulates into an FP32 register, then a shared-memory tree reduction over the 256 partial sums writes one output. Mirrors the dequantize-then-FP32-dot fallback path in runtime/src/inference/ops_transformer.rs (the Q8_K-quantized activation fast path used by vec_dot_q4_k_q8_k isn't portable to GPU without a Q8K_QUANTIZE kernel, deferred). Validated within 5e-4 relative tolerance across all distinct Qwen2.5-1.5B SLM matmul shapes (Q/KV/up/down); worst observed relative error was 1.02e-6, well under tolerance. Source: scripts/cuda/q4k_dot_f16.cu (#540).

Fused Grouped-Query Attention decode step: out[hq, d] = sum_t softmax(Q[hq] · K[t, hq/group] / sqrt(hd))[t] * V[t, hq/group, d]. Three phases in a single kernel per Q head: QK-dot + max-reduce, numerically-stable softmax, attn-weighted V sum. GQA pairing via group = n_head_q / n_head_kv (Qwen2.5-1.5B uses g=6, Llama-2 g=1 = MHA, Mistral g=4, MQA g=n_head_q). Limits: head_dim ≤ 256, seq_len ≤ 4096 (kernel uses ~17 KB shared memory; both caps comfortable for every shipping SLM context length). Mirrors runtime/src/inference/ops_transformer.rs::gqa_decode_step. Validated within 8 ULPs across Qwen2.5-1.5B (seq_len 1..2048), Llama-2 MHA, Mistral GQA, and an MQA-hd64 fixture; worst observed was 1 ULP at every shape, and the seq_len=1 boundary case (softmax of one logit → out = V[0, hkv]) is bit-exact. Source: scripts/cuda/gqa_attn_f16.cu (#540).

Token-ID → embedding-row gather over a Q4_K-packed embedding table. The first op of every SLM forward pass; produces the FP16 input vector for the first attention block. One block per super-block in the row, 256 threads per block — same Q4_K decoding path as q4k_dequant_f16 (#699) plus a token_id-keyed row offset and an embedding_length bounds check that handles padded rows (e.g., SmolLM2-135M's 576-element rows stored across 3 256-element super-blocks = 768 dequantized; only 576 written). Mirrors runtime/src/slm/forward.rs::embedding_lookup_any. Validated bit-exactly across Qwen2.5 (1536), Llama-2 (4096), Phi-2 (2560), and the SmolLM2 padded-row boundary. Source: scripts/cuda/embedding_q4k_f16.cu (#540).

future_entries.comment: Add these when their kernels land. Documented here so the manifest reads as a roadmap, not a punch-list.
future_entries.GEMM_GENERIC.HMMA.FP32A_FP16W: from #661/#676 — gemm_hmma_fp32a_fp16w_shader.sass. Mixed-precision (FP32 activation × FP16 weight) GEMM used by the MNIST FC layer when it has to consume an FP32 pool2 output. Schema gap: today's (op_kind, tier, dtype) triple can't express the activation-vs-weight precision split — needs a schema bump (separate `act_dtype` + `weight_dtype` fields, or a packed dtype-pair encoding) before this can move into `entries`. The MNIST launcher (scripts/gpu-kernel-mnist.c) loads the SASS directly via --shader-dir today, bypassing the operator library, so this is dormant until the schema lands.
future_entries.Q4K_GEMM.SIMT.Q4K: multi-row Q4_K matmul for prefill — same per-output-row kernel as Q4K_DOT but tiled across multiple input rows. Until it lands, prefill chunks dispatch Q4K_DOT once per row.
future_entries.Q8K_QUANTIZE.SIMT.FP16: FP16 → Q8_K row quantizer. Unlocks the vec_dot_q4_k_q8_k fast path that the CPU reference uses (~2× the dequant-then-FP32-dot path's perf on CPU; expect similar on GPU).
future_entries.GEMM_GENERIC.HMMA.BF16: tensor-core BF16 if a target model wants it
future_entries.GEMM_GENERIC.IMMA.INT8: future quantized matmul on tensor cores
